name: Asian Paints Ltd
about: Asian Paints is the largest home decor company in India. The 80+yr old company has major brands like Asian Paints, Apco, etc under its umbrella. The co. is into wall paints, wall coverings, waterproofing, texture painting, wall stickers, mechanized tools, adhesives, modular kitchens, sanitaryware, lightings, soft furnishings, and uPVC windows.

flags.text: Operating cash ran at 109% of reported profit over five years.

business.summary: Asian Paints manufactures and sells decorative paints, coatings and related services to retail, professional and B2B customers across India and internationally, earning revenue from product sales and value‑added services.

segments.name: Decorative paints
segments.note: Core revenue driver; highlighted in AR Business Review.

segments.name: Premium segment (All Protek)
segments.note: Growth focus via premiumisation and Lotus Effect technology.

narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Operating margin fell to 17.7% FY25 before recovering to 18.8% FY26.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Premiumisation will upgrade consumers to higher‑value products.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Revenue declined 4.3% YoY in Q1 FY27 and FY25, indicating limited premium uptake.
Cash from operations rose to ₹7,088 cr FY26, showing strong cash generation from service mix.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Regionalisation tailors offerings to diverse Indian markets.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Working‑capital days improved to 38 days FY26, suggesting better regional inventory management.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Backward integration will fund profitable growth.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Debt/Equity remained low (0.1‑0.2), supporting capacity to invest without leverage.

bull.point: Operating margin rebounded to 21.4% FY24 after a dip, indicating margin recovery.
Cash conversion averaged 109% of profit over five years, showing high quality earnings.
Debt/Equity stays at ~0.1, reflecting a strong balance sheet.

bear.point: Revenue fell to ₹33,906 cr FY25 after a peak in FY24, signaling demand weakness.
Operating margin dropped to 17.7% FY25, the lowest in the six‑year window.
Cash from operations slumped to ₹986 cr FY22, indicating volatility in cash generation.

synthesis.one_line: Strong cash conversion and low leverage mask a recent revenue and margin slump.
